### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a0f865491d365d1447e45d1efd27a251e6e6c181` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9209480b119e087ae317fc0d96d54a1c932764f8` — the merge of head `fb157ea75512ac8c1057763339dee196c6a88a6a` into base `a0f865491d365d1447e45d1efd27a251e6e6c181`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9209480b119e087ae317fc0d96d54a1c932764f8 && git checkout 9209480b119e087ae317fc0d96d54a1c932764f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a0f865491d365d1447e45d1efd27a251e6e6c181 fb157ea75512ac8c1057763339dee196c6a88a6a && git checkout -B drift-repro a0f865491d365d1447e45d1efd27a251e6e6c181 && git merge --no-ff fb157ea75512ac8c1057763339dee196c6a88a6a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a0f865491d365d1447e45d1efd27a251e6e6c181
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); `view.zod.ts` moved on `main` since the merge-base, in hunks the diff does not touch.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The new TSDoc paragraph is true of the renderer** - right. Since #28291 (`85a1b9d8`) `kanbanDeclaredLanes` maps the declared list onto columns in the author's order, an unlisted value falls into `Uncategorized`, and an absent or empty list returns undefined so the board keeps one lane per option in the options' own order. The paragraph says exactly that, and the `.describe()` text at :2102 already said it, so the shipped reference page does not change (docs-drift found no hand-written anchor to move; `check:generated` is green in `Lint · docs & code guards`).
- **The lint docblock line is true of the rule** - right. `checkKanbanLanes` reads only `optionValues`, which is built from each field's inline `options[].value` and nothing else, so a future `FieldSchema` key that widens what `groupByField` may carry would report a lane naming a widened option as unknown until it joins that map. That is rider S2 of record 6528382115 on #28211, placed on the function docblock as the card and the order asked.
- **Accept-set: nothing an author writes moves** - right. No schema, type, export, message string or refinement changes; the diff is two comment hunks and a changeset. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec` patch, no `@objectstack/lint` entry** - accepted. The lane's precedent for a TSDoc-only change whose text ships in the built package (`dist` chunks and `src/**/*.zod.ts` are in `files[]`). The lint docblock is not in its built `dist` by the dev's measurement (a message string from the same function is, as the positive control), and this review does not re-measure it; if the lint build ever starts preserving docblocks the omission is a changeset gap, not a contract gap.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Serial overlap on `view.zod.ts`** - `main` moved the file after the merge-base (other keys); the merge is clean and no hunk is shared, so nothing is owed beyond the usual merge of `main` before landing.
- **The seat lands** - `domain:ui#1` holds the card under the cross-area rule; no Tier H path (no `docs/adr`, no `skills/**`, 49 lines), no human gate, no name approval owed.
- **Nothing further** - the stale sentence has no other copy in the tree (the dev's `git grep` and this review's read of `content/docs` agree).

**Verdict reasoning.** A false sentence about a live key is replaced by the behaviour the merged producer has, matching the describe text that already ships; the lint docblock gains the one line a prior review asked for; a patch entry covers the one shipped surface; the head is clean against `main` and every check is green or skipped.
